newsitem.title: USA: US spot resids mostly hold with crude, LSFO gains.
newsitem.headline: US spot resids mostly hold with crude, LSFO gains.

text.p: U.S. spot fuel oil prices mostly held steady on Wednesday in lackluster trade, but prospects for some utility interest, particularly in Florida, left low sulphur more buoyant, market sources said.

"It's pretty quiet but the market feels at or close to bottom. There's been some utility interest and one percent is probably up a little," said one cash trader, noting that the mostly mild East Coast weather stalled demand.
In New York Harbor, physical one percent edged up slightly to $16.50-$16.75 a barrel, with June-July one percent paper done early at $16.85, also modestly higher, traders said.
Traders said NYH June and July one percent paper quotes were now in the $16.85-$17.20 area, with August talked at $16.75-$17.00.
NYH 0.3 percent high pour notionally held steady, with fairly prompt FOB barrels still pegged in the low-$17 area.
High sulphurs in New York were unchanged, with three percent delivered sellers in the $15 area.
At the U.S. Gulf, one percent again firmed slightly to $16.25 or higher on prospects for some Florida utility demand.
USG three percent was little changed at $14.25-$14.50, with June three percent paper reportedly done at $14.35 and $14.50, up more than a quarter on the day.

New York city gate swing gas prices firmed slightly to about the $2.50/mmBtu area, or $15.75 a barrel equivalent. Gas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, was up a few cents to $2.33/mmBtu, or $14.68 a barrel.
